name: MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD

sources.note: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

purpose: Xiaomi states: the MOPD upgrade of MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL; it fuses several domain-specialized teachers into one model (including domains where training-time verification is hard) and mitigates a failure mode in which the model keeps issuing the same tool calls without progress. Agentic, multimodal (text, image, video, audio), 1 M context.

lineage.how_derived: multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD2) on top of the RL checkpoint, plus a short specialized-teacher run against tool-call repetition

license.name: MIT (card tag; no LICENSE file in the repository)
license.notes: Card YAML says mit; the repository has no LICENSE file and the card has no license section, so the text could not be read.

architecture.kind: sliding-window + global attention MoE with vision and audio encoders
architecture.gguf_arch: mimo2 (name in the ggml-org repo not verified)
architecture.attention: 39 sliding-window layers (window 128, 64/8 heads) and 9 global layers (64/4 heads), head dim 192 (V 128); first block global with a dense FFN
architecture.drafter: 5-layer SWA MTP/DFlash-style drafter predicting 7 tokens (separate GGUFs in the ggml-org repo, 1.3 to 5.4 GB)
architecture.why_this_design: The card gives the layout (SWA with 128-token window plus few global layers, MoE without shared experts) but no reasons; the long-context cost argument is not stated in the text read. Reasons for MOPD2 and the repetition fix are stated (see purpose).

variants.notes: ggml-org is the llama.cpp project organization; not Xiaomi

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (105.9 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 9% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (105.9 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 13% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

engine_support.notes: GGUFs, MTP and DFlash drafters are in the ggml-org repo; Tona would need a new module (SWA-128 + global layers, head dim 192/128, 256 experts without shared expert).

strengths: Users report direct, consistent agent behaviour and a test step at the end of its own work
Small KV cache: 39 of 48 layers have a 128-token window
Drafters shipped (DFlash 45 to 47 tok/s on code on a 128 GB Strix Halo)
weaknesses: Coding scores are not on the card (they are in the technical report PDF, not read)
Smallest official-format GGUF is 106 GB: only 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class machines
No Artificial Analysis entry for V2.6-Flash (only MiMo-V2-Flash at 49.8 and V2.5-Pro at 60.2)
soft.behavior: Tool-call repetition was a known failure of the RL checkpoint; the MOPD checkpoint is the fix according to Xiaomi (response-level repetition rate chart in the card).
best_for: agentic coding on large unified-memory or 128 GB RAM machines
soft.maturity: Xiaomi MiMo: third generation of the family, technical report for V2.6; 26k downloads of this repo, 5 discussions.

user_reports.summary: Used the ggml-org MXFP4 GGUF in an agent harness (about 216 GB RAM at 131K context): more direct and precise than Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, always adds a testing step; the Q2_K also good, speed better than GLM-4.7-Flash
Strix Halo 128 GB, Vulkan: requantizing the attention (Q4_K) gives +17 % decode (26.2 to 30.7 tok/s) at KLD 0.027; DFlash 45 to 47 tok/s on code at 1K and 41 to 43 at 31K

tona_fit.reason: MIT by card, good user reports on agent behaviour and a small SWA KV, but the card carries no coding benchmark, the license text is not available and the smallest GGUF (106 GB) fits only the 32 GB + 128 GB class. Revisit when the technical report numbers are read.
blockers: Tona has no module for this SWA/global layout (engine support, not a quality judgement)
